newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish group rivals Hachette for Ruch news-stands.
newsitem.headline: Polish group rivals Hachette for Ruch news-stands.

text.p: A group of Polish investors has placed an offer with the prime minister and privatisation ministry to buy state-owned press distribution chain Ruch SA, a member of the group said on Tuesday.

Jozef Birka, board member of private television network Polsat which is one of the investors, said the group aimed to acquire 40 percent of Ruch, while 40 percent would be offered to the public and the state treasury would retain 20 percent.
"An informal group of investors has been set up...including such firms as Bank Rozwoju Exportu SA (BRE) Multico, the Sports Totalisator, Radio RMF...," Birka told Reuters.
But BRE spokesman Jaroslaw Celski declined to confirm that the bank was taking part.

The PAP news agency quoted Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz as saying this group's bid was "considerably better" than an existing offer from a consortium linking France's Hachette press distributor and Polish companies.
Cimoszewicz told reporters the Hachette consortium's offer for Ruch was "clearly below a reasonable level", PAP said.

Polsat's Birka said that if the new group was successful in acquiring a stake it planned to invest $200 million to $250 million in Ruch, which would be used among other things to build 4,000 newspaper kiosks and replace vehicles used for distribution.
He said participation of the state-owned Sports Totalisator, which operates the national lottery monopoly, would lead to construction of 3,000 kiosks selling lottery tickets and newspapers.
The Zycie Warszawy newspaper, published by mineral water firm Multico which is one of the bidders, said on Saturday the consortium would offer about $120 million for Ruch.

The rival consortium of Hachette, Polish publisher group UWP and other firms are seeking more than 50 percent of Ruch. French President Jacques Chirac is likely to support this consortium's case when he visits Poland in September, the daily said.
News-stand chain Ruch, which controls about 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market, had a net profit of 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995.
It has about 17,000 news-stands and was the country's sole press distributor before the 1989 fall of communism.

Initially Poland offered up to 75 percent of Ruch but in March Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek cancelled the tender and offered a minority stake, with an option to increase the equity -- prompting Swiss firms to pull out of the Hachette-UWP group.
Kaczmarek said in May he was unhappy that only one investor ended up bidding for Ruch.
